course_name_original: DINAMICA E CONTROLLO DEI SISTEMI ENERGETICI M (87260)
course_name_en: DYNAMICS AND CONTROL OF ENERGY SYSTEMS M

learning_outcomes.text: Describe an energy system using mathematical models.
Study its behavior in terms of stability and response to external stresses.
Define control strategies in order to condition the response to improve its quality and compliance with technical specifications.

syllabus_topics: Frequency response of linear systems: Bode diagrams, Nyquist plot
Open and closed-loop systems: Definition and evaluation of permanent errors.
Definition of margin of phase and amplitude.
Stability of a closed-loop system: Nyquist stability criterion.
Compensation of the disturbances in feedback systems by means of lead and lag Compensators and standard regulators.
Hydraulic, mechanical and thermal systems and components.
Application of control theory to power plants (steam turbine, hydraulic turbine, turbogas), cogeneration plants, heat production plants, internal combustion engines
teaching_methods: Frontal teaching lessons in the classroom with blackboard
Examples, exercises and practical applications using openSource software (e.g. Octave, Scilab, python, Hopsan) or commercial (such as Matlab / Simulink, AMESim)

assessment_methods.method: Analytical / numerical solution of exercises to be carried out at home

assessment_rules: The final exam is a written test of approximately 3 hours, consisting of two parts: a written test in the classroom on theoretical topics and an analytical/numerical solution of exercises to be completed at home. The exercises are made public on the day of the written test and must be returned within two days. The exam is graded from 0-30, with 18 being the minimum to pass. If part of an integrated course, the final grade is the arithmetic average of marks from constituent courses, rounded to the next whole number; '30 e lode' (30 and honors) is awarded if 30 is obtained in both modules and honor in at least one.
